title: Cocycle of the canonical pro-etale quotient reductions
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative coefficient ring in the independent coefficient universe, J an ideal, and N any pro-etale derived constant A-module. Use the normalized reductions N_i, scalar extension E_h, reassociation s and quotient isomorphisms rho of [lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data]. For all r >= m >= n, including equalities, E_(m,n)(rho_(r,m)).hom followed by rho_(m,n).hom equals s_(r,m,n).hom at N_r followed by rho_(r,n).hom. No etale origins, markings, completeness or constructibility are involved.

source.place: Tag 09C2 quotient reductions; explicit normalized balancing of parent proof steps 1 and 4; Tag 06YY.

proof.text: Transport the normalized ordinary scalar comparison to each specified composite ring map. Three applications of the ordinary tensor adjunction show that maps out of a threefold scalar extension are determined by successive insertions of one. On these insertions, the normalization of adicFiniteChangeComp and tensorSection_map prove the ordinary cocycle. This argument includes equal quotient indices.

Lift the ordinary cocycle degreewise to cochain complexes. Prove an abstract pasting identity: after postcomposition with the final invertible computation map, the four normalized composition formulas reduce the derived cocycle to the ordinary cocycle. Naturality of the intermediate computation map and intermediate derived comparison gives the two required middle interchanges.

Use resolving_nat_ext on the flat-term K-flat resolving class. The K-flat resolution theorem supplies the resolving class and change of rings preserves that class. Apply the pasting identity on each representative using adicFiniteExtendCompFormula; the final computation map is invertible. Thus the two derived natural transformations agree at every derived object.

Package derived coherence as an equality of whole natural isomorphisms, then specialize to the three constant sheaf maps induced by the quotient at r and the quotient factors r to m and m to n. The given quotient composition identities supply the four specified composites. A generic category lemma takes components and substitutes the named reductions and rho isomorphisms using their defining equalities. This obtains exactly the displayed equation without unfolding chosen comparison maps across the coefficient-universe specialization.

lean.statement:
theorem adicReduction_cocycle (X : Scheme.{u})
    {A : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (N : adicFiniteAmbient.{u, v} X A)
    (r m n : ℕ) (hnm : n ≤ m) (hmr : m ≤ r) :
    (adicFiniteExtension (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X)
      (adicFiniteFactor J hnm)).map (adicFiniteRho.{u, v} X J N hmr).hom ≫
        (adicFiniteRho.{u, v} X J N hnm).hom =
      (adicFiniteExtensionComp (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X)
        (adicFiniteFactor J hmr) (adicFiniteFactor J hnm)
        (adicFiniteFactor J (hnm.trans hmr)) (adicFiniteFactorComp J hnm hmr)).hom.app
          (adicFiniteReduction.{u, v} X J N r) ≫
        (adicFiniteRho.{u, v} X J N (hnm.trans hmr)).hom
